issues.cell: law 1 (10)'s "a line a commit lays or moves (its laidAt or courseAt that commit's)" x law 2 Entry's and The soft readings' "a meeting made after its lock" x Order's keepers (a re-section, a Deck height or Arch spacing edit, an undo; no redo) x the check's (10) x law 4's undo dependency clause; C13, W14; veto 23
issues.claim: Law 1 (10) bars a shape-held thing's soft readings only from a line a commit dates, and Order lets a re-section, a Deck height, Arch spacing, width or class edit and an undo keep their dates (a redo is named neither way). So (i) a Deck height lowering or an Arch spacing edit over a shape-locked ring cuts its run lower or merges an aqueduct into it, (ii) a re-section whose wider band crosses a shape-locked aqueduct's vault-use span opens it, and (iii) an undo of a wall's delete (or a redo of its drawing) made after the lock re-creates the meeting with its old laidAt and opens the vault again - all lawful by (10) and invisible to the check (no record field, no new date) - while Entry and The soft readings bar any soft reading from 'a meeting made after its lock', veto 23 has the later thing bend or give way, J149's application says a shape-locked wall is never merged into, and J147 (3) says the shape-locked wall never changes. Builder A applies each edit and the undo (the shape-locked thing changed, against J147 in (i)); Builder B bends or refuses them, the lock dependent. The redo's laidAt (the target's seq or the redo's) and law 4's dependency clause (unconditional, or only where law 1 fails) split again; §7.4's independence does not decide it (the lock's touched set is disjoint from the delete's).
issues.required_change: Part L law 1 (10): replace the date-only bar by 'a shape-held thing takes no soft reading from a meeting a commit after its lock makes or deepens - one where that commit lays or moves a line (its laidAt or courseAt that commit's), re-creates a structure or a line (an undo, a redo, a revert), or changes the other side's section, band, width, deck height, stations, spans or class (a re-section, a Deck height, Arch spacing, width or class edit) -: no wall-like line, band or strip newly across the strip of a vault-use span of it, no aqueduct newly merged into it, no soffit newly or further lowered over a run of it, no gate made in it; the readings it had when the commit began follow what stands only as the other side falls, decays, is repaired on its own course, is removed or moves off'; Entry and The soft readings: 'a meeting made after its lock' -> 'a meeting made or deepened after its lock (law 1 (10))'; the check: '(9) and (10)'s later lines by the laidAt and courseAt the commit wrote' -> '(9)'s later lines by the laidAt the commit wrote, and (10)'s by the laidAt and courseAt it wrote, each structure or line it re-created and each section, width, deck height, station, span or class it changed (its undo record)'; Order: 'an undo (which restores the record)' -> 'an undo (which restores the record) and a redo (which re-applies its target's record, its lines dated as the target dated them)'; law 4: 'a later live event whose structure the re-created meeting would meet counting as dependent' -> 'where law 1 would not then hold, each later live event whose structure, or whose lock, the re-created meeting would meet counting as dependent'; veto 23: 'laid or moved after the user locked' -> 'laid, moved, re-sectioned, re-valued, or re-created by an undo or a redo after the user locked'.

issues.cell: Placement ('with the places of its gates, posterns and towers', PRB7E-GEN-09) x law 1 (10)'s 'a thing held in placement keeps its placement' x the check's (10) x Carried way's gate in a placement-locked wall (G2, E-D6, E-D7 'gateMade', E-S2, E-V9-4) x The soft readings ('a gate Carried way makes by hand ... follows of itself from what stands') x Tier 1; T110-4 (c)
issues.claim: A raised road drawn by hand into a town whose ring the user placement-locked: Carried way, (G2), E-D6 ('its placement kept'), E-D7 and E-S2 make the gate as a soft reading of that wall, but pass 5's Placement lists a wall's gate places among its placement fields, law 1 (10) keeps a placement-held thing's placement, and the check and T110-4 (c) compare those fields unless the event names the wall - it names the road. Builder A makes the gate and fails E_INVARIANT on every placement-locked ring a raised road enters; Builder B keeps (10) and re-routes the carried way to a standing gate, else refuses. Separately, The soft readings make that gate a reading that 'follows of itself from what stands', while Carried way has §7.3's S7 operator write a Gate record that Tier 1 never moves: when the road is deleted, re-shaped so its carried way crosses 40 m along, or the user has drawn streets through the gate, the gate stays (a record, an orphan beside the new one) or vanishes (a reading, breaking those streets, an unshown change of a held placement since a delete is no meeting). Two outcomes in each case on the commonest hand gesture into a walled town.
issues.required_change: Part L Placement: '... with the places of its gates, posterns and towers' -> '... (a gate Carried way makes in a placement-locked wall by hand among them - the one change of a held placement a meeting makes, J144's soft reading of that wall, shown by law 4's (G2))'; law 1 (10): 'a thing held in placement keeps its placement' -> '... keeps its placement (but for a gate Carried way makes in it by hand)'; The soft readings: strike 'and a gate Carried way makes by hand' from the readings and add 'A gate Carried way makes by hand is no move either, so law 3 never ranks it, but it is no reading: §7.3's S7 operator writes it, and from its commit it stands as every gate does (Tier 1) - kept when its carried way is removed, re-routed or re-shaped off it, as a declared way's gate is (§7.3's S7 row), its own event's undo alone removing it'; the check: 'unchanged unless the event names it as its own target' -> '..., a gate Carried way made in a placement-locked wall excepted'; T110-4 (c) (E-S13): 'every locked structure's placement' -> '... (but for a gate a raised road's carried way makes by hand in a placement-locked wall)'.

issues.cell: the tiers (Tier 1 'never moved by a meeting') x law 2 (a)'s 'each thing it lays or places - a gate, postern or tower of its own along its own wall's line' x correction 1 x A warp and veto 22 x W14 and veto 18 x the bent group's (iv) x the castle by hand x the check (no clause for a Tier-1 thing's place)
issues.claim: A standing gate or tower that the op's own edit carries or re-derives into a strip - a run re-traced from a moved trace vertex (§7.3's S7 operator re-making 'a gate at each declared crossing'), a warp, a re-section's re-derived gatehouse (W14), a retaining wall's chain grip, a castle's bailey grip - is either a thing the op 'lays or places' (law 2 (a) slides it clear along its line, its road following by (b); law 3 key (1) prefers this as it keeps the value the op set; the bent group's (iv) and the castle's 'claim moving whole' read so) or a Tier-1 thing 'never moved by a meeting' (the drag bent back along its drag, a warp refused since never halved, the re-section refused - W14 and veto 18 read so). Veto 22 says both ('kept clear by its own course - a standing one it meets never moved'). A vertex drag beside a viaduct, a warp and a re-grade each have two outcomes, and no bar sees which: law 1 has no clause for a Tier-1 thing's place and the check's (10) compares one only when held (pass 5's verdict asks this).
issues.required_change: Part L the tiers, after 'is never moved by a meeting': add '- nor by the meeting an op's own edit makes: a gate, postern or tower that stood when the op began and that its own edit carries or re-derives (a run re-traced from a moved trace vertex, a warp, a re-section's re-derived gatehouse or tower, a retaining wall's chain grip) stands where that edit puts it, and law 2 (a) bends the op's given shape round it instead - a dragged vertex or grip back along its drag, an edited value to the nearest that keeps it clear (law 3), a castle's claim moved whole by its siting with its gate and towers on it - else law 2 (c), a warp refused (A warp: never halved)'; law 2 (a): 'each thing it lays or places - a gate, postern or tower of its own along its own wall's line' -> 'each thing it newly lays or places, or whose own grip the user slides - a gate, postern or tower of its own along its own wall's line (one S7 lays by spacing on a stretch the op lays, S5a's pin, a gate the user places or slides, a gate the op makes where a ground way crosses its new line)'; law 1 new (11): 'every gate, postern, tower and fixed place standing when a commit begins stands at its end where it stood, where an op naming it or its wall put it, or where the tiers leave it (J148)', the check adding '(11) by each gate's, postern's, tower's and fixed place's place the commit touched against its undo record'.

issues.cell: law 2 (a)'s local bound and 'an end back along its own line' (PRB7E-LCK-01) x law 3 key (1)'s 'one that re-lays it (which an op does only where it names that course or trace - a stroke, a re-shape, a drawn course)' x Order (a re-shape dates what it moves) x law 1 (3); veto 2; C13; down before the wall by hand; PRB7D-LCK-09; J148 tier 2
issues.claim: A viaduct the user drew stands; a ring laid later passes beneath it ungated. A 3 m drag of the course vertex beside that crossing re-dates the stretch over the ring (Order), so law 1 (3) bars the deck there; a drag that carries a stretch across a standing ring is the same. Builder A follows key (1) (keep the value the op set; a re-shape may re-lay its course), PRB7D-LCK-09 ('a stretch dragged across a standing ring comes down before it'), veto 2 ('it comes down before the wall, its road going on through a gate beyond the foot'), C13 and down before the wall: the deck is cut before the ring and its far part becomes a ground way through a new gate - a nudge demolishes the viaduct beyond the ring, no local bend of the newer structure (against J148's 'the newer one bends locally'). Builder B follows (a)'s bound (the far end is not a thing the re-shape lays; the cut is no local re-lay) and veto 2's own 'one whose two ends are fixed is not built': the drag bent back along its drag, and where any drag re-dates the crossing, refused. Two outcomes on the commonest raised-way edit beside a walled town; PRB7E-LCK-01's bound no longer admits the cut PRB7D-LCK-09's closure relied on.
issues.required_change: Part L law 2 (a): 'an end back along its own line' -> 'an end the op lays back along its own line (a stroke's, a drawn course's or a frame growth's extension's; never an end of a standing deck that a re-shape, a warp or a revert leaves where it stands)'; law 3 key (1): 'before one that re-lays it (which an op does only where it names that course or trace - a stroke, a re-shape, a drawn course)' -> 'before one that re-lays it beyond law 2 (a)'s reach, which no lawful shape does (J148: the newer bends locally)'; Order, after '... date what they move': add '- save that a stretch they move which, at the commit's end, still crosses a run it crossed when the commit began, under the same span or at the same support, keeps its former date at that crossing -'; veto 2: 'a re-shape re-laying only the stretch it moves' -> 'a re-shape, warp or revert that would carry a stretch of a standing deck newly across a wall is bent back along its drag, else refused'; C13's 'a re-shaped road deck stretch across a standing trace bent down before it' corrected the same.

issues.cell: law 1 (2) (J149: 'an enclosing wall's line meets an aqueduct's strip only to cross its deck line') x law 1 (3), (4), (7) x the strip (stripMarginM, 1 m) x correction 3 x the bent-group sentence's strip, (ii), (iii) x veto 4 x E-S4 x T-V9-52 (E-V9-2)
issues.claim: Law 1 keeps a wall from running along a strip only by law 1 (2), which tests the line of an enclosing wall against an aqueduct. A hand drawWall along beneath an aqueduct is moved by law 2 (a) only to just outside the 1 m-margin strip, so its band (2-3 m each side) runs under the arcade's edge for the whole run, through every pier, its own top above the soffits (law 1 (7)) - in no form, since over and merged are read 'there', at the crossing. Along beneath a road deck, or ending under either deck, no clause of law 1 is false at all (law 1 (3) speaks only of a crossing; (7) caps), so the stroke is lawful as drawn. The bent group's (ii)-(iii) (its strip widened by the band's half), veto 4 ('no wall runs along beneath an aqueduct or ends under it'), E-S4 ('its band outside the under-deck strip') and T-V9-52 ('a wall drawn along beneath the viaduct moves to the strip's edge') move both. Builder A follows the laws (an along-band under an arcade with no form; a wall kept along beneath a viaduct); Builder B follows the examples and tests. Two maps on the commonest along-beneath gesture, and none in the aqueduct case. J149 replaced pass 4's band test with this line test.
issues.required_change: Part L law 1 (4): 'no enclosing wall's line, band or wall strips lie over a raised way's ends' -> '...; and an enclosing wall's line, widened each side by its band's half there (§4.8), lies in a raised way's strip only where it crosses that raised way's deck line - entering on one long side, leaving by the other, meeting the deck line once there -, never running along within it, entering and leaving it on one side, or ending in it'; law 1 (2): 'an enclosing wall's line meets an aqueduct's strip only to cross its deck line - entering on one long side, leaving by the other, meeting the deck line once there - and crosses it' -> 'an enclosing wall's line crosses an aqueduct's deck line (law 1 (4))'; veto 4 and the bent-group sentence's (ii)-(iii) cite law 1 (4).

issues.cell: law 1 (5)'s 'but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears its top' (J149) x §4.3's crossing rule ('within ± squareDeg of square to the deck, never along the strip') x placeGate's stub ('square to it') x W13 x Block 2 row (b)'s gates cell x correction 7 and Part H's head
issues.claim: Where a ring crosses an aqueduct square to its deck line under an arch that clears a gatehouse, law 1 (5) admits a gate there (J149's over; Part H's head keeps every END from moving it), so a placeGate at that at, or a street drawn across the ring there, keeps its gate (law 3 key (1)). But a gate's passage crosses the band square to the wall and placeGate's stub is square to the trace, so the gate's way runs along the deck - along the strip into the piers - which §4.3's crossing rule bars, and Block 2 row (b) puts such a gate out of the strip. The laws read the gate, never its way. Builder A keeps the gate and its stub fails the crossing rule's row; Builder B moves the gate out by row (b) against law 1 (5) as Part H's head reads it; Builder C finds no lawful shape and refuses. A gate under an arch has a way only where the wall crosses the deck line within squareDeg of parallel to it (the Porta Maggiore form), which the laws never say.
issues.required_change: Part L law 1 (5): 'but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears its top, never on a support's ring' -> 'but under an aqueduct whose every span over it clears its top - and, for a gate, whose strip the way through its passage crosses by §4.3's crossing rule (under one span, within raisedWays.structure.squareDeg of square to the deck, never along the strip), so that a gate stands under an aqueduct only where its wall crosses the deck line within that angle of parallel to it -, never on a support's ring'; correction 7's reading and Part H's head: 'a gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing under the aqueduct only where its spans clear it' -> '... only where its spans clear it and, for a gate, its way passes (law 1 (5))'.

issues.cell: law 2 Carried way's 'through the nearest gate that wall has along its line' (PRB7E-LCK-03) x meeting's and the tiers' 'gates (posterns, water gates and a harbour-mouth chain among them)' x 'a postern, which has no way' x §5.3's gate row; veto 12
issues.claim: A raised road drawn into a town whose ring the user shape-locked: its carried way is re-routed 'through the nearest gate that wall has along its line', else the stroke takes law 2 (c). Part L defines a wall's gates as including posterns, water gates and a harbour-mouth chain, none of which a road passes. With a postern 40 m along, a water gate at 90 m and a main gate at 180 m, Builder A re-routes to the postern, §7.3's S4 operator finds no route through it, and the stroke is refused; Builder B re-routes through the main gate. Two outcomes for a raised road into a shape-locked town, by canvas and clerk alike; the same split for a gate of a lesser class.
issues.required_change: Part L Carried way: 'through the nearest gate that wall has along its line' -> 'through the nearest gate that wall has along its line which a way of the carried way's class may pass (§4.8 Gates; never a postern, a water gate or a harbour-mouth chain)'; veto 12 the same.

issues.cell: correction 7's list x law 1 (5) x Part H's head; R7-02: over the band's strip clear of gates and towers, No gate and no tower, the bent group's (iv), W1·C1, W2·C2, W13·C2, Block 2 row (b)'s gates cell, attack 7, the paths note's bend.wall.aqueductArch line

issues.cell: E-S13's T110-4 (c) and E-S0's C8 second run x law 1 (10) and shape as pass 5 refined them x the check (outline and size) x correction 6
issues.claim: T110-4 (c) asserts 'every shape-locked one's shape, unchanged by every op that does not name it', but shape now holds the soft readings and the chamber, and law 1 (10) lets the readings from before follow what stands (deleting the wall under a shape-locked aqueduct's open arch lays its chamber, PRB7E-LCK-04), so the bar fails a correct build; the check compares outline and size only. E-S0 runs C8 'on a second run shape-locked' and says 'Each run takes its cell', the C8 cell being the unheld one read by correction 6 as placement-locked - a later wall across the shape-locked way's vault-use span, its chamber removed - which law 1 (10) bars.
issues.required_change: Part H E-S13, T110-4 (c): 'every locked structure's placement, and every shape-locked one's shape, unchanged by every op that does not name it' -> 'every locked structure's placement, and every shape-locked one's outline and size, unchanged by every op that does not name it, and no shape-locked one taking a soft reading from a meeting made after its lock (§2.7's laws, law 1 (10); The check)'; E-S0, after 'Each run takes its cell of §2.7's crossing table' add '- the shape-locked C8 run its cell as §2.7's laws, law 1 (10), leave it: the later wall or raised way bent clear of what the lock holds, else refused, waiting or not built (law 2)'.

issues.cell: law 2 (a)'s 'by its own derivation' x the support step's (3) band obstacle (kept by E-M1's sweep) x correction 3 x J149 applied's Merged x Part H's head x E-S1 (T110-2 (1))
issues.claim: A hand aqueduct is laid 'by its own derivation', and the support step's (3) still slides a station off an enceinte's band, else omits it, a merged span past maxClearSpanM bending or refusing a declared course; E-M1 keeps that list. J149 applied says merged removes every case of a support slid off a band and of an aqueduct refused for want of a course whose supports keep off it, correction 3 says a support is kept off by nothing, and Part H's head rewrites E-S1's refusal ('across a wall where no course keeps its supports off the band within maxClearSpanM, refused') as that correction reads it - built, merged. The law with its derivation and the rewritten test give two outcomes for one stroke; the law governs, so the test is the example to correct unless the derivation's list changes.
issues.required_change: Part L correction 3, after 'a support is kept off by nothing (law 1 (2), (3): a road deck's laid through, an aqueduct's merged; J149)' add '- the support step's (3) taking no enceinte's band as an obstacle to an aqueduct's station, so that no aqueduct's own derivation slides, omits or bends for a band (E-M1 writes (3)'s band clause "an enceinte's band, for a road deck's station")'; or, keeping the derivation, Part H's head's 'an aqueduct refused, not built or waiting for want of a course whose supports keep off a band' struck from its list, E-S1's refusal standing.
